channel.title: PINtPRESS
channel.description: Long-form writing from the PINtPOINT team on beer, pubs, and the tools we build. Postcards from beer cities, guides to crawls and styles, and notes on what's new in the app.

item.title: A Cider of His Own
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Jeffrey House spent ten years selling other people's cider in America, losing Fuller's to Grolsch and Blackthorn to Miller. So he made one of his own, sold 1,200 cases of it to a supermarket before he had bottled a drop, and built ACE into a brand he would be hired back to rescue.

item.title: The First Friday of Christmas
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Tuborg's Julebryg goes on sale at 20:59 Danish time on the first Friday of November, and not a minute before. A Norwegian king once made Christmas brewing compulsory, and in 1975 Fritz Maytag brewed one in San Francisco that, as far as he could discover, was the only real one in the world.

item.title: Winter is not Christmas
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: A winter beer and a Christmas beer are different things. In 1971 Young's renamed an old Burton ale Winter Warmer, four years before Fritz Maytag walked round the brewery looking for something else.

item.title: Voice of the Fire
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Harvey's have brewed in Lewes since about 1820 and on the Ouse since 1838, make Bonfire Boy for the fifth of November, and ferment it with a yeast that came down from York by train in 1957. In 2006 the regulars boycotted their own pub when Greene King took Harvey's off.

item.title: Roast is not smoke
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Harvey's use black malt to give Bonfire Boy its suggestion of smoke. Black malt comes from an 1817 drum, taken from coffee roasting, that gave brewers colour with the fire kept off the grain.

item.title: Season of the Witch
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The Green Man carvings are medieval, the pub name is centuries old, and the pagan reading only dates from 1939. On folk horror, Rentaghost, pumpkin ale, green hop beer and cider at Halloween.

item.title: The Unholy Trinity
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Three of autumn's great nights fall inside a single week: Halloween, Lewes Bonfire, and J-dag, when Tuborg's Christmas beer goes on sale. In each one something that looks old turns out not to be. Three essays, publishing 26 October, 2 November and 6 November.

item.title: Before he could sell ESB to America, he had to sell it to Fuller's
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Jeffrey House remembers the first pour: Fuller's ESB on draught at the College Inn in Seattle on 3 November 1987. He had been trying to get it there for years, and when it arrived American brewers found more in it than a good pint.

item.title: Why Firestone Walker chose Fuller's yeast
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Firestone Walker's beer trials picked the Wyeast strain Walker remembers as a Fuller's ESB yeast over Chico, the workhorse of American craft, even though Chico was cleaner. Then its flocculation handed them diacetyl at packaging. What replaced it is still, in co-founder David Walker's words, essentially a Fullers/London yeast. Fuller's head brewer of eighteen years says there was never an ESB yeast at all.

item.title: Tegernseer on Draught in the UK: Eleven Venues We Can Confirm
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Tegernseer Hell is one of Bavaria's most sought-after lagers and reaches British bars in small, unpublicised quantities. Cross-referencing our own live tap data finds eleven UK venues that have poured Tegernseer, from The Rake at Borough Market today to a Nottingham bottle shop and a Hertford free house with three of them at once. Sorted by how recently each was actually seen, not by how recently anyone claimed it.

item.title: Everything Traditional About Oktoberfest Is Younger Than the Tent
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: In 1898 five strawmen for a Munich brewery won five Oktoberfest stalls, and Nuremberg publican Georg Lang joined them into a hall for 6,000. The other restaurateurs sued the city and lost.

item.title: UK Oktoberfest Events 2026
item.description: Munich tapped the first keg at noon. Seventy-six British Oktoberfests, sorted by the only question that matters: is the beer in the stein actually from the Wiesn?

item.title: September is Oktoberfest
item.description: The 191st Wiesn opens tomorrow at noon. Munich moved from amber Märzen to pale Festbier between 1953 and about 1990, and one tent still pours the old beer from the wood. America kept the amber, and Britain treats the whole vocabulary as a licence.

item.title: Cask Ale Week: the Cellar, the Plaque and Thirteen Pints
item.description: Cask Ale Week runs 17-27 September: what cask is, what the Perfect Pint Promise covers, thirteen pints worth chasing, and the numbers behind a revival led by younger drinkers.

item.title: The Geography of Sobriety
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: How the move of Fleet Street's papers to Wapping in 1986 and the growth of Canary Wharf from 1988 changed where London's journalists and City workers drank.

item.title: Old Haunts of the Square Mile
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Balls Brothers, Corney & Barrow, Davy's, All Bar One and Pitcher & Piano: five City bar chains of the 1990s, and what became of their sites.

item.title: Ghosts of Baddow Brewery
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Baddow Brewery stopped brewing in 1927. Nearly a century later, 30 of the 61 pubs associated with it are still serving drinkers, scattered from Great Baddow out to the Essex coast. Fourteen have been replaced or converted, fifteen have gone, two remain honestly unknown. And a stone's throw from the old brewing ground, Chelmsford Brewing Company has brewed at Brewery Fields since 2017.

item.title: These aren't revivals. They're not even spirits
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: British beer is having a revival revival. Old names are back on the bar: some painstakingly reconstructed, some entirely new beers wearing dead men's clothes. Divers and KU Leuven are trying to recover the yeast DNA from an 1864 Guinness shipwreck bottle. A field guide to what's actually being resurrected: recipe, yeast, water, brewery, people, badge, or nothing but the name.

item.title: Davy's: a century and a half of sawdust and candles
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Founded off the Strand in 1870, Davy's still lists fifteen London sites of its own, fourteen of them trading, plus three El Vino sisters brought in in 2015. In 2007 the chain had 37 sites; more than half of the family-name ones have gone since. Bangers, Bangers Too, the Crusting Pipe (closed just before Christmas 2025 after a 45-year run), the City Boot twice, City FOB, Skinkers, and two different lives of the Tappit Hen. The story of a chain slowly editing itself down.

item.title: Celebrity-Owned Pubs Worth the Pint (Not Just the Autograph)
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: News this week that James Blunt has bought a second London pub, The Carpenter's Arms in Hammersmith, is a decent excuse to ask the only useful question about celebrity-owned pubs: which are actually worth the pint? Verdicts and PINtPOINT deep links for Ian McKellen's Dickens-listed Thames boozer, Blunt's Chelsea local, Guy Ritchie's Fitzrovia gastropub, Jeremy Clarkson's Cotswolds farm-pub, and seven more.

item.title: The Green Triangle and the Oldest Trademark in British Beer
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: On 1 January 1876 Britain's first registered trade mark went to a beer: Bass Brewery's red triangle, UK Trade Mark No. 1, signed off by Registrar Henry Reader Lack at 47 Chancery Lane. A hundred and fifty years later, to the year, PINtPOINT needed a shape to single out the best pub around. What else could we pick? Why the geometry, why green not red, and why on a small screen at the end of a long day the fastest way to say 'this one' is still a triangle.

item.title: The Anti-Check-In: Why We Skip the Feed
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Untappd is a social network first and a beer database second. Its tap lists only get fresh when someone posts publicly about a pint. PINtPOINT lets you improve any tap list with one tap and no check-in: no feed post, no badge, no requirement that you actually drank the beer. Why fresh tap lists shouldn't depend on social posting, and why the gap between 'I drank this' and 'I saw this' compounds.

item.title: It's Not Just the Sunshine: Your Holiday Beer Really Is a Different Beer
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The Estrella you drank in Barcelona is not the strength of the Estrella they pour in Manchester. Damm bought the Bedford Eagle Brewery from Carlsberg Marston's in 2022 and brews a 4.6% UK version of the 5.4% Spanish original there. Madri Excepcional is brewed at Tadcaster in Yorkshire. What CAMRA's July 2026 Beer in the UK Report exposes about the lagers on every British bar, and why calibrating your PINtDEXTER against a holiday beer isn't the same as calibrating against the version poured in your local.

item.title: The Beer Final We Almost Had: England vs Spain · The Parallel-Timeline Pub VAR Verdict
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Argentina beat England 2-1 in the semi-final on Wednesday. This piece was drafted for the beer final we might have had: a Berlin rematch of English cask against Spain's Iberian craft column. Publishing it anyway as the parallel-timeline read. Draught Bass hat-trick, a 101st-minute ghost goal, Estrella Damm and La Pirata Black Block. The Pub VAR booth stands by its verdict. The actual final (Argentina vs Spain) follows in a separate piece.

item.title: Norman Balon: London's Last Great Rude Landlord
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The Coach and Horses landlord who ran the Greek Street pub for sixty-three years and made a public brand of his own rudeness has died aged 99. On the fortnightly Private Eye lunch, the Waterhouse play, the 2005 licensing regulations he wouldn't sit down and read, and why a room isn't the same room once the person who kept it wrong on purpose has gone.

item.title: Humphrey Smith: British Beer's Great Awkward Character
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The Samuel Smith's beer baron who ran Britain's strangest pub chain by his own private rule has died aged 81. On cheap pints, dark wood, shire horses, boarded-up villages and a row over an air freshener, and on why the whole thing may become easier without him and also less peculiar.

item.title: Loaded's World Cup Canon: From Crisps to Vodka and erm, a selection of more questionable items
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The canonical record of Loaded magazine's recurring World Cup format. The first five editions ran in fifteen months from September 1994 to December 1995, through Crisp, Washing Powder, Lager'lympics, Cereals and Vodka, and define the format at its peak. The canon then carries on through Toast, Ice Lolly, Booze, Stockings, Art (hosted by Tony Hart), Sex Toy and Meat (presided by Mark Gatiss as Hilary Briss) until January 2001. Bylines, winners, the through-lines.

item.title: Lager'lympics: Loaded Magazine's Lost 1995 Lager World Cup, Found
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The full record of the Lager'lympics, Loaded magazine's 1995 Lager World Cup, published in the 'What's For Tea Love?' food and drink supplement. 62 lagers, knockout bracket, drunk-panel scoring. Budvar won the final 178–98 against Molson. Loaded's own archive doesn't carry it; PINtPOINT has scanned the bracket.

item.title: Before Kick-Off: Why English Cask Has the Advantage
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The football is heading to the business end. The Beer World Cup is heading the same way. With the Perfect Pint Promise just launched and heritage cask back on the rise, the case for English cask is loud and current. Greene King has sold Old Speckled Hen to Spanish lager giant Damm, Draught Bass is back on more than a thousand hand pumps, and JW Lees has relaunched cask Boddingtons. The squad of eleven hand-pulled pints we'd send into a Beer World Cup, the moat argument that says cask is the one format the world can't quite copy, and a forward-look to Cask Ale Week 17–27 September.

item.title: World Cup 2026 Stadium Beer Map: Help Us Find Good Beer Near The Grounds
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: A first-pass map of bars, pubs, breweries, taprooms, bottle shops and beer gardens around all 16 World Cup 2026 host stadiums across the USA, Canada and Mexico. Some host areas came together cleanly. Some are awkward. First pass, not the final whistle. Open PINtPOINT near a host stadium and add what we missed.

item.title: Beer World Cup XI: 48 Nations, Real Fixtures, Stupidly Serious Beer Results
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The football teams play on the pitch. The beers play in the pub. Every country in the World Cup gets a beer squad; the actual draw drives the matchups, and Pub VAR may upset the scores. A serialised editorial tournament loosely based on a distant memory of Loaded magazine's lost Beer World Cup.

item.title: Beerology: The Anatomy of a Pint
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: What does this beer actually feel like to drink? Eight axes (Body, Bitterness, Sweetness, Roast, Fruit, Finish, Softness, Complexity) plus four drinker cues, a drinkability bucket and one plain-English gut-take sentence per beer. Built for the 800-millisecond tap-list decision; honest about the sour and Belgian-yeast styles it doesn't cover. Capstone of the four-essay arc on choosing the right pint.

item.title: Following the Firkin trail(s)…
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: In 1979 David Bruce opened the Goose & Firkin in Elephant and Castle. By 1995 the chain had 44 pubs, 19 of them brewing on site. On 8 October 1999 the brewing stopped, and that, not the 2001 brand-discontinuation, is when Firkin actually died. By 2001 the brand was gone too, but the buildings (mostly still pubs under other names) outlived it. The 12 original London Firkin sites deliberately traced the outline of a dog's head on a 1990 paper leaflet. Companion: walk the Firkin Ale Trail Hall-of-Fame crawl in PINtPOINT.

item.title: Anchor Brewing's British heritage runs deeper than people realise
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Two of Anchor's signature beers came home from an October 1975 English brewery tour. Liberty Ale, the one everyone credits to it, predates the trip by six months on David Burkhart's dating. The Great American Beer Festival was modelled on CAMRA's GBBF. Anchor first reached British draught in November 1991, in borrowed Fuller's kegs, and a West Yorkshire distributor kept it there for fifteen years after. The companion to Friday's piece on Anchor's revival: the case that Anchor's identity was always partly English, and what that means for a return to UK taps.

item.title: Anchor Brewing looks to be coming back. Nobody will say when.
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Construction crews at Potrero Hill, an owner who has said almost nothing in public, and a 2027 date nobody official has given. Updated in November with the label approvals and the business-name filing.

item.title: Under the Hood: How PINtDEXTER Picks Your Pint
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The engineering follow-up to PINtPOINT's beer-recommender essay. The four layers PINtDEXTER stacks under the hood (preference capture, manual sliders, per-beer LLM-inferred flavour DNA, and venue-aware scoring), plus the misclassified pale lager that exposed the most recent fix. References yhat's 2013 R prototype and Kushwaha's 2023 LLM-on-comments work to trace the 2013 to 2026 arc of beer recommendation.

item.title: Save Our Pubs, In One Pub: The Bell at Ingatestone
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: We walked into the Bell at Ingatestone on Saturday to claim a free pint of Telegraph Ale. PINtPOINT's Financial Pressure Index also flags the same building as Struggling: rateable value +74% since 2023, FPI 44.38/100. The Save Our Pubs campaign's structural argument, made personal, on the bar in front of us.

item.title: Almost Two Pubs a Day Are Closing. The Telegraph's Answer Is a Free Pint.
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Saturday 16 May 2026 is The Telegraph's National Pub Day. Renegade Brewery, the West Berkshire outfit that took on the West Berkshire estate after the 2023 collapse, has brewed Telegraph Ale, a 4% English bitter, for cask delivery to nearly 300 participating pubs. The campaign sits inside Save Our Pubs, the Telegraph's response to a closure rate the paper put at four pubs a day.

item.title: From Half of British Beer to Half a Percent: What Happened to Mild
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: In 1959 mild was still half the beer Britain drank. By 2011 it was 0.5%. How Britain's everyday beer became a rarity, and why Mild May is trying to bring it back. Pattinson, Cornell and Boak & Bailey on the collapse from a 1700s young-ale category through the 1930s peak to the post-war floor; the modern fork between Black Country stalwarts at 3-3.5% and craft revisionists at 6-10%.

item.title: The Sparkler Question: A Field Guide to Britain's Quietest Cask Argument
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: A small nozzle fitted to the end of a cask tap reshapes your pint: head, mouthfeel, perceived bitterness. 140 years of British cask argument, mostly a Northern tradition with London outposts at the Queen's Arms and the Punch Tavern. From 14 May 2026, the Whippet adds Boddingtons cask with a sparkler to the Liverpool Street commute.

item.title: The Whippet at Liverpool Street
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The Whippet still is not pouring Augustiner, but it has quietly built one of the more unusual lager line-ups near Liverpool Street: Bitburger, Kutna Hora, Tegernseer and Benediktiner, alongside Boddingtons cask through a sparkler. Only the Tegernseer is brewed in Bavaria.

item.title: Radio City Turns 7: 7 Cans, 7 Sins, 35 Launch Venues, and One Big Saturday in Chelmsford
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: On Saturday 9 May 2026, Radio City Beer Works marks its seventh birthday with a brewery party in Radley Green, preceded by the nationwide can release of The 7 Deadly Sins on Thursday 7 May across 35 first-pour venues UK-wide. Brewery party logistics, full sin × brewery × style line-up, and the launch-venue locator.

item.title: Blackhorse Beer Mile 4th Birthday: All 10 Participating Venues with PINtPOINT Links
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: On Sunday 3 May 2026, Walthamstow's brewery-district mile turns four with an all-day, free-entry, family-friendly takeover across 10 east-London craft venues. Every participating venue with a PINtPOINT deeplink plus the canonical Hall of Fame crawl.

item.title: Augustiner on Draft, Finally: Six Confirmed UK Pubs Pouring It
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Augustiner Helles launched on UK draught in November 2025 via James Clay & Sons with no public venue list. PINtPOINT cross-references public Untappd data to confirm six UK pubs pouring it, across London, Manchester, Glasgow, Knaresborough and Worcester. The Whippet, flagged for it at its May opening, is expected but not pouring it yet.

item.title: 12 Years of Bosko: All 12 UK Venues Pouring Pressure Drop's West Coast IPA on 1 May 2026
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Twelve years of Pressure Drop's iconic West Coast IPA, celebrated 1 May 2026 with simultaneous pours at 12 UK venues. Full launch-venue list with PINtPOINT links and back-story on Bosko.

item.title: Left Field Beer and the Price of American Craft in Britain
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Fresh American imports (Trillium, Hop Butcher), European specialists (Arpus, CoolHead, Factory) and championed UK indies (DEYA, Buxton), curated from a single Solihull shop, with the deep-dive on why drinking American craft properly is so expensive over here.

item.title: Bass Pale Ale: The Red Triangle That Took an English Beer Global
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Before consumer brands were global, Bass already was. The red triangle of Bass Pale Ale travelled to India, Russia and America in the 19th century, riding hard Burton water, coke-malted pale grain and clear glass into a worldwide reputation. The story from 1777 through the Bass Charrington years, the Molson Coors split, and modern attempts to recover Burton pale ale heritage.

item.title: A Postcard from London: From Porter and IPA to the Kernel
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: London is one of the oldest beer cities in the world, but the version you can drink now dates from 2009. The third in the postcard trilogy: a comeback layered over an inheritance.

item.title: Walking the Ted Lasso Pub Trail in Richmond: From Crown & Anchor to Richmond Hill
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: The Crown & Anchor exterior is The Prince's Head on Richmond Green. One stop is a Richmond Hill finisher with the kind of Thames-bend view the show keeps coming back to. A four-stop walking pub trail for fans of the show, and a shortlist of the wider Richmond craft-beer scene worth a pint while you're there.

item.title: A Postcard from Melbourne: The City That Built a Craft-Beer Scene on Bars, Not Breweries
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Companion to the San Diego piece, and its structural opposite. Catfish, Local Taphouse, Cookie, Hippo, Boilermaker: a scene that turned curation into a category of its own.

item.title: The Drinker's Guide to Hops: What Each Variety Actually Tastes Like
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: A drinker-first reference to the 30-odd hops you're most likely to meet on a UK or European bar (Cascade, Citra, Mosaic, EKG, Saaz and the rest), organised by a six-category flavour framework.

item.title: A Postcard from San Diego: Where the West Coast IPA Grew Up
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: Karl Strauss in 1989. Stone and Ballast Point in 1996. A hop arms race through the 2000s that perfected the West Coast IPA. A tour of how San Diego quietly became the IPA capital and where to drink its legacy today.

item.title: The Chelmsford Beer Mile: A Live Guide to the Route
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: When we wrote this, eight specialist venues sat within a mile of each other (bottle shops, a brewpub, railway arch taprooms). This guide walks them in the right order, with live tap lists for every stop, plus a footnote on Baddow Brewery (1798–1927) and the forty-year gap before Chelmsford Brewing Company started up in 2017.

item.title: What's Wrong With Beer Recommendation Systems (And What PINtPOINT Does Differently)
item.dc:creator: PINtPOINT
item.description: A response to Ethan Haley's Untappd-as-a-recommender analysis and NYC Data Science's Ninkasi project. Three walls rating-based recommenders hit (cold start, popularity bias, geography-blindness) and how PINtDEXTER layers around them.
